newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent follows NYMEX WTI down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent follows NYMEX WTI down on profit-taking.

text.p: IPE Brent crude lost ground on Monday in line with losses on NYMEX WTI crude. Profit-taking on NYMEX led Brent down to the lows of the day, brokers said.
The November Brent contract traded down at $23.17 a barrel by 1513 GMT, down 30 cents on the day, matching the losses on the November WTI contract.
"Brent is just following WTI (NYMEX), there's no fresh market-moving news," one broker said.
Meanwhile, fundamental demand and speculative trading saw October IPE gas oil better supported, trading up $4.75 at $233.25 a tonne, just off the high of $234.50.
The contract saw upside resistance at $235 a tonne, with support at $232 followed by $228.75.
NYMEX front month product contracts expire on Monday but brokers did not expect heating oil to take the brunt of any profit-taking.
"Heating oil is not the place to sell in this market. I don't expect it to go off too weak. The low (U.S.) inventories and an open arbitrage to Europe make it fundamentally strong," one said.
